$schema: Provider cooldown profiles for free providers
$doc: Research-based cooldown values. Providers that return Retry-After headers can have shorter base cooldowns.

groq.notes: RPM: 30-60, TPM: 6K-30K, per-model. Verified 2026-09-27: the free-plan limits table is keyed by MODEL ID with distinct RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD per row. IMPORTANT: 'Rate limits apply at the organization level, not individual users' — so a second Groq API key does NOT grant a second quota, it only avoids per-key auth/rate-limit bookkeeping. Headers: x-ratelimit-limit-requests (always RPD), x-ratelimit-limit-tokens (always TPM), -remaining- and -reset- variants, plus retry-after only on a 429.

nvidia.notes: RPM: ~40. Often missing Retry-After. Be conservative. UNVERIFIED limit_scope: NVIDIA's API reference carries no per-model limits table, so this stays per-key. Verify with scripts/probes/limit-scope-probe.py before changing.

cerebras.notes: Verified 2026-09-27: 'Rate limits apply at the organization level, not the user level, and vary based on the model'. The Limits-by-Tier table is keyed by model id (gpt-oss-120b 5 RPM/30K uncached TPM, qwen-3.8-27b 1 RPM/5K uncached TPM), and both the uncached and total TPM buckets are per model — a 429 body says which bucket was exceeded. CAVEAT: there is NO permanently free tier any more. The 'Free Trial' is $5 of credits expiring in 30 days, and it requires a verified payment method. A 402 here means the trial expired, and auth/credit failures are always global cooldowns, so this upstream will eventually hard-fail rather than degrade.

poolside.notes: Free preview tier: 200 requests/hour (matches local_quota_for in catalog.rs). Poolside's rate-limit docs are access-gated, so limit_scope is UNVERIFIED and left at the per-key default — deliberate, because the damaging error is a wrongly-shared bucket. Verify with scripts/probes/limit-scope-probe.py before changing it.

sambanova.notes: Free tier is PER-MODEL: 20 RPM / 20 RPD / 200K TPD for each model individually (DeepSeek-V3.1, Meta-Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, gpt-oss-120b each get their own 20 RPM). Docs page: 'SambaNova model rate limits'. Note the TPD is per-model on the free tier, while Developer tier is capped at 20M tokens/day ACROSS all models. Headers: x-ratelimit-limit-requests, -remaining-requests, -reset-requests, and -day variants.

zai.notes: Zhipu AI GLM. Conservative estimate pending research.

mistral.notes: Docs: 'Completion rate limits are listed per model' — each model gets its own tokens-per-minute and requests-per-second limit, viewable at admin.mistral.ai/plateforme/limits. Free mode exists ('lets you create API keys and use included monthly usage'). NOTE: the same page says rate limits 'define how much traffic your Organization can send', so keys in one Organization share a quota — but that is a property of the USER'S key set (how many Organizations their keys span), not a per-provider constant, so nothing is encoded for it here. See docs/free-model-routing.md section 8.

google.notes: Verified 2026-09-27: 'Limits vary depending on the specific model being used' and 'Rate limits are applied per project, not per API key'. So model scoping is correct, but a second Gemini API key from the SAME project shares the quota — only a second project grants a second quota. RPM/TPM/RPD vary by model and tier; RPD resets midnight Pacific; RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED signals exhaustion.

cloudflare.notes: MIXED scope, left per-key. RPM is per TASK TYPE (Text Generation 300 RPM, Summarization 1500, Embeddings 3000, ASR 720) with some per-model overrides such as @cf/baai/bge-large-en-v1.5 at 1500; paid-model limits 'apply per account, per model'. But the 10K neurons/day quota is cumulative per account, and a single limit_scope string cannot express both — so this stays per-key until learned per-model bucket state lands. Returns error codes 3036/3040.

openrouter.notes: MIXED scope, resolved as per-model. Per-model RPM ('different rate limits for different models, so you can share the load that way'), so a rate limit on one model leaves the others usable. The free-model DAILY quota is a different signal and is gated by all-time credits purchased, which is cumulative per account — but that surfaces as a 402/credit error, and 402 is deliberately NOT an exhaust signal (it is treated as a display-only negative balance, per key_rotating.rs), so it never becomes a wrongly-scoped cooldown here. ALSO GLOBAL ACROSS KEYS: 'Making additional accounts or API keys will not affect your rate limits, as we govern capacity globally' — a second OpenRouter key buys a second spending cap, not a second quota. Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset.

cline.notes: MEASURED 2026-09-27. Each of the 6 models in the recommended-models `free` array has its OWN daily counter; one model hitting its cap does not affect the others. A cap returns 429 INFERENCE_CAP_ERROR 'Daily free limit reached on model <id>. Try again in 20h 54m'. Requires the X-CLIENT-TYPE: cline-sdk header (already sent in production) or every free id 403s with 'only available via Cline product surfaces'. Works at zero credit balance - 402 insufficient_credits is a PAID-model gate and does not block the free ones. cline-pass/* needs a ClinePass subscription (403 ENTITLEMENT_ERROR) and cline-cloud/* is unsupported.

hedging.notes: Based on Google's 'The Tail at Scale' paper. 100ms delay optimal for most scenarios.

p2c_selection.notes: Power of Two Choices: reduces peak connections by 30% (Cloudflare research).

adaptive_concurrency.notes: Netflix gradient-based approach. Disabled by default for stability.
